question.text: An organic compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>]</mo><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, shows optical activity and gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> gas on treatment with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>HNO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>]</mo></math> reacts with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>PhSO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>Cl</mi></math> producing a compound which is soluble in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KOH</mi></math>. The structure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is :

solution.text:
Given:
1. Compound is optically active ⇒ contains chiral carbon/Nitrogen.
2. Compound liberates N2 gas with HNO2⇒ It is primary amine
3. Compound reacts with PhSO2Cl and the product is soluble in KOH - It is a primary amine.

Option (A) and (D) are primary amines. But only option (D) satisfy all the above conditions.
